plan.title: Hallmark GSEA: psoriasis lesional vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is functional, not gene-level: differential expression is already done and delivered as de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns, treated psoriasis lesional vs control), so the plan adds no new DE model. Per the Inflexa procedure for enrichment on a delivered results table (R-0110@41cb), the plan (1) verifies the delivered counts' sample structure before relying on the contrast, because counts.csv is also delivered and sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, and (2) runs a preranked fgsea GSEA of the full 12,000-gene list against the 50 MSigDB Hallmark human sets (v2026.1, staged at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt). Ranking metric is the disputed choice (R-0108@409f); this plan chooses the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) — signed, scaled by its standard error, tie-free — over unshrunken log2FC (noise on low-count genes) and signed -log10 p (saturates and ties). Genes and the Hallmark GMT are both HGNC symbol space, so no identifier remapping is needed beyond an overlap check with the unmapped share reported. fgsea 1.38.0 and DESeq2 1.52.0 are installed. A final report step pins the collection version, rank metric, tie rule, and leading-edge genes per significant set, and states that enrichment findings are method-dependent hypotheses.

steps.method: vst blind transform + PCA on top-500 variable genes + sample distance heatmap + library size check (DESeq2)
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) against MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1
enrichment report with leading edge, reproducibility record, and method caveat
